CCL integration plan/request (source-only, no cross-owner edits): current ACPI
Snapshot_Provider endpoint also controls snapshot upload/start/finish, so it must
not be distributed to arbitrary CCL handlers. ACPI-owned next slice is a pure
bounded polling client with authenticated reply correlation, copied observation
assembly, and explicit broker delivery confirmation before ACK. Trusted provider
polls downward, then schedules handlers after the call returns. No callbacks in
the ACPI request loop, no logger changes, no new hardware authority.
CCL/native binding and launcher owners will need to coordinate a nominal event
schema/import or typed task and trusted endpoint distribution. Current catalogue
has no ACPI binding. Plan only for CCL_Native_Bindings/native-runtime-services and
launcher/procmgr catalogue; no edits authorized in those owned areas here. If
separate consumer authority is needed, design it explicitly rather than widening
Observer or giving handlers the Snapshot_Provider endpoint. Detailed reviewed
plan: ../.acpi-proof-work/acpi-notify-consumer-binding-plan-4ahs10tc/PLAN.txt.

## Exact receiver claim reconciliation

Receiver.Receipt returns the exact originally claimed notice,or absent for an
unused/rejected delivery. It does not attest handler success,cleanup or hardware
quiescence. Redispatch of a consumed Delivery cannot produce a receipt for a
different payload. A fresh duplicate Delivery has no receipt of its own.

Publisher.Confirm_Claim accepts only Delivery_Unknown,an exact retained notice
(controller,epoch,token,event number),and the full authenticated sender matching
the independently provisioned Expected_Consumer. Default No_Process disables
receipt acceptance. Sender must come from kernel receive metadata; these are
internal APIs,not a wire format or a source of hardware authority. Receipt loss
still retains the notice; reliable receipt transport/retrieval remains native
integration work. All entry points must remain serialized and nonreentrant.

Acceptance releases publication metadata only. It performs no EC transaction,
enqueue or AML invocation,and never clears receiver Field uncertainty,result
roots or catalog hardware recovery. Ready means publication can progress; the
catalog still rejects requests while retained for recovery.

An excessive charge stops further notices and attempts cleanup without clamping the report. A refused or uncleared release remains owned by the session; Pending/Close allow cleanup in the original Core lifetime, including after region or method changes. Foreign cleanup is refused. Successful cleanup never reconnects a failed session or replays _REG. The session, Core and backing must remain alive while Pending is true; hardware/provider withdrawal is a separate owner decision.

The old code demonstrably lost its cleanup handle after an overcharged returned package. The new portable tests/acpi-region-cleanup passes948checks/40processes across both AML widths and checked/release; existing alias/region/orphan regressions pass3668checks/94processes. Two older source lists gain their missing resource-name/device-status dependencies. ACPICA matches explicit alias method effects/package values; its cache-cleanup diagnostic is retained, and provider fault/lifecycle equivalence is not claimed. Callback ownership/release contracts remain trusted. No new SPARK proof or native/hardware validation; native provisioning and the full verified service/interpreter remain unfinished.

## Bounded drain after EC serving stops

Controller.With_Receive.Drain now permits one bounded owning advance after a serving stop, without receiving queues, invoking event/control hooks, submitting new work or idle waiting. It requests stop before advancing. Precommand work can stop without writes; postwrite exchanges retain their original budgets/deadline and may finish or remain in recovery. Pre-existing serving adapter/owner/reentry/unexpected-reply faults and new drain faults quarantine the route. Repeated calls never reopen serving or replay replies/publications. Advanced is not quiescence or permission to exit/release backing. The lifecycle owner must retain engine/controller, saved replies, authority and recovery until independently resolved.

The EC owner defers service receive during active bounded hardware work,allows control access during retained recovery,gives a Field opportunity between query episodes,and suppresses idle wait only for runnable queued work. The default hook preserves old controller behavior. These are serialized scheduling rules,not native latency or global quiescence guarantees.

## Bounded EC query scans

Request_Query_Scan is an opt-in, independently admitted source-hook request. One
FIFO entry remains until an accepted query observes SCI_EVT clear or returns zero.
Each distinct query consumes one allowance and keeps its original finite request,
pause and publication budgets. A scan waits through publication backpressure or
unknown delivery; exact claim or explicit publication retry settles only that
notice. No failed/unknown hardware query or handler is automatically replayed.

Scan_Exhausted retains the head entry without polling hardware or blocking Field
and control requests. Trusted Resume_Query_Scan supplies a new allowance only
after successful exhaustion, not during accepted work, publication retention,
failure or stop. The serialized supervisor must arrange a subsequent turn/wake.
Later FIFO entries stay behind the scan; direct source Start_Query cannot bypass
it. One Field opportunity separates iterations. Stopped drain can settle only an
already accepted scan iteration and never starts another query.

Observe.Scan reports head phase/remaining allowance and a historical empty-query
response. No_Head_Scan or a past empty response is not global quiescence. Source
authority, masking/GPE completion, command-wide ownership or held Global Lock,
backing lifetime and all upper AML/notification obligations remain independent.
This does not re-enable a source, release backing or launch native hardware mode.

## Status-only field lookup failures

A failed field lookup now propagates only a payload-free failure status. Success, module-completion or bare fatal statuses supplied in a Failed_Binding response are refused as Unsupported_Value; that response carries none of the corresponding result data. This corrects the generic executor callback boundary. The concrete namespace readers did not produce those invalid statuses in the accepted field tests, and valid field-read behavior is unchanged.
